title: Introduce KMS revocation-fuse and audit-replay safeguard
author: Aisha Kumar
description:
Motivation: rapid incident response for suspected key compromise requires an operator-level ability to temporarily freeze tenant KMS usage without deleting keys or changing customer config. Existing region-pin and KMS-scoping controls handle placement and residency, but there's no safe operational 'fuse' that gates signing/encrypt operations while preserving forensic audit trails. This PR adds a low-risk revocation-fuse primitive and an auditor-facing replay-safeguard for immutable audit segments.

Summary of changes: single continuous description string with checklist and high level details.
- Add KMS revocation-fuse service (revocation-controller) that flips a tenant-scoped fuse flag. When fused, KMS calls return a controlled error code (KMS_TEMPORARY_FUSED) and are routed to an enforceable fallback path in the serving runtime. The fuse is time-bound and requires an operator-signed token to clear.
- Extend audit pipeline with sealed segments: when a fuse event occurs the pipeline generates an immutable sealed-audit segment containing request/response digests and operator metadata; sealed segments can be replayed by investigators using time-limited replay-tokens that are emitted by the audit service.
- RBAC v2 additions: introduce a new scoped role operator.kms.fuse with minimum privileges and a policy template for emergency-fuse workflows. Update role mappings and policy simulator tests.
- Residency/region interaction: ensure fuse operations are honored regardless of region pin; add cross-region signal to replicate fuse state to active failover replicas within the residency bounds.
- Observability: add metrics (kms_fuse_events_total, kms_fuse_active_count), tracing tags (fuse.operator_id, fuse.reason) and dashboard tile.

- [x] Security review: SEC-1120 signed off (see reviewer thread).

- feat(audit): sealed-audit segment generator + replay-token endpoint
- perf(runtime): fast-path for KMS_TEMPORARY_FUSED and graceful fallback to cached-wrapped-key path
- chore(rbac): role template and simulator test cases
- docs: operator runbook and console tile instructions

Files changed (high level):
- services/kms/revocation_controller.go (new) -- core fuse state machine + API
- services/kms/handlers.go (mod) -- integration hooks and error codes KMS_TEMPORARY_FUSED
- runtime/kms_adapter.go (mod) -- fast-path handling and fallback strategy code comment added
- audit/sealed_segmenter.py (new) -- creates sealed segments with digest+operator metadata and stores to sealed-audit S3 namespace
- audit/replay_service.go (new) -- mint replay-tokens scoped by investigator id and time window
- rbac/templates/operator_kms_fuse.yaml (new) -- role template for operator.kms.fuse
- docs/runbooks/operators/kms-fuse.md (new) -- operational steps and post-mortem checklist

Small illustrative snippet (runtime fast-path): ``if err == KMS_TEMPORARY_FUSED { return ErrFuseActive } // caller triggers fallback`` (kept intentionally concise).

Review conversation (condensed into chronological thread):
- Linda Park (review): "Nice minimal surface. Please ensure the replay-token audience is one-time and can't be used to extract raw key material."
- Aisha Kumar (author): "Replay tokens are scoped to sealed-audit object IDs, include nonce+expiry and require investigator cert via mTLS. Added tests in audit/replay_service_test.go to prove token revocation on expiry."
- Marco Ruiz (review): "What happens if the operator mistakenly unfuses? Can we add an undo audit event and an automatic cooldown?"
- Aisha Kumar: "Added cooldown config (default 1h) and an explicit operator.reason field that is required for unfuse; we log undo events to sealed segments too."
- Sasha Ivanov (security): "Simulate cross-region replication -- ensure fusion state doesn't break residency guarantees."
- Aisha Kumar: "Added cross-region signal logic with residency guard; fuse replication is only broadcast to replicas within the tenant's residency zone (see revocation_controller.go)."
- CI: initial lint failed on audit naming; fixed. Integration pipeline passed; security scan flagged a missing KMS permission in a test role which was corrected. Final CI status: pass.

Operational notes and runbook summary:
- Fuse semantics: time-bound (configurable), operator-initiated, tenant-scoped. Intended for suspected compromise / emergency halts. Not for routine deployments.
- Audit guarantees: sealed segments are append-only, content-addressed (sha256), and stored under sealed-audit/<tenant>/<segment-id>. Replay tokens allow read-only access to a single segment for a limited window and are issued by the audit service after operator request with justification.
- RBAC: operator.kms.fuse is intentionally narrow; plan to gate in RBAC policy bundle for SOC2 environments.

Release notes: "Add emergency KMS revocation-fuse primitive and sealed-audit replay safeguard. Operators can temporarily freeze tenant KMS usage while preserving immutable audit artifacts for investigation. Includes RBAC templates and runbook."

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after approvals from Linda Park and Sasha Ivanov.

Follow-ups (post-merge):

- SEC-1203: threat-model audit of replay-token lifecycle and HSM usage for sealed segment signing.
